affirmation.author: Brandon Payton <brandon.payton@a8c.com>
affirmation.behavioral_safety: At ABI 55 Kandelo syscall 304 (klogctl) was absent from the declared contract: it had no entry in syscalls, syscall_arg_descriptors or channel_scalar_contract, and the kernel answered every call with a fake success, returning 0 and leaving the caller's buffer untouched. An ABI-55 program could issue 304 all the same, because __NR_syslog was already in bits/syscall.h.in and musl's src/linux/klogctl.c compiled, so its argument slots were decoded with the default i32 kind. Two things therefore change for such a program, and both are safe. First, the one kind the new entry declares is {index 2, u32}: the same slot's same 32 bits read unsigned instead of signed, so the sole reinterpretation is the sign of a length argument that previously could not affect the answer at all. Second, the call now does something: it reads the kernel message ring instead of returning 0 with the buffer untouched. An ABI-55 program could only ever have observed that hardcoded 0, which nothing can usefully depend on, so replacing it with real behavior cannot regress one.
